body:

I do see:

```
Jun 26, 2019 12:35:08 PM io.quarkus.deployment.QuarkusAugmentor run
INFO: Quarkus augmentation completed in 1158ms
```

printed _after_ openapi scans things (in the test that fails), but before ORM loads the classes (in the test that works)

@stuartwdouglas or @dmlloyd any idea how I can fix this?
SmallRye OpenAPI actually uses jandex, but they check if the entity is a subtype of `Collection`, which is not in jandex and so they revert to loading the class.
So we could fix this by making SmallRye OpenAPI use a throw-away CL, or making the extension depend on a build marker that says that types have been instrumented. WDYT?
Or we get `Collection` and `Map` in the index. Can we do that?
Fix in #2987 but not sure it's the right fix.

issue.title: RestEasy + Panache + OpenApi: did you forget to annotate your entity with @Entity?
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
When I add the openApi dependency to the project I get:
This method is normally automatically overridden in subclasses: did you forget to annotate your entity with @Entity?

**Expected behavior**
No error

**Actual behavior**
Stacktrace:
java.lang.IllegalStateException: This method is normally automatically overridden in subclasses: did you forget to annotate your entity with @Entity?

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1: https://github.com/andrejpetras/quarkus-quickstarts/tree/bug-openapi-panache/hibernate-orm-panache-resteasy
2. https://github.com/andrejpetras/quarkus-quickstarts/commit/4fa8d6f85745408b52e6dc8b549d828e5a9c6f31
4. mvn clean install
5. remove the openApi dependency

Also I have a issue if the ElementCollection was LAZY
```
    @ElementCollection(fetch = FetchType.EAGER)
    @CollectionTable(
            name = "PARENT",
            joinColumns = @JoinColumn(name = "PARENT_GUID")
    )
    public Set<String> parents = new HashSet<>();
```

body: If you have an ordering constraint, then that should probably be represented by a build item dependency.  I have a change (#2952) which introduces "virtual" build items but just producing and consuming an empty simple build item is probably good enough for now.  I think it does make sense to have a build item representing the fact that bytecode enhancement was completed.
I'd be fine with that, except I think the augmentations are done lazily so not sure we can determine they've all been done. Also I suspect they're done outside the build graph…
OK, I just merged the fix.

issue.title: Reduce the occurrence of reflection for many known cases

repository.name: smallrye-open-api
repository.description: SmallRye implementation of Eclipse MicroProfile OpenAPI

issue.body:
Relates to #191 and also the fix for quarkusio/quarkus#2961.

The idea with these changes is to mostly eliminate the fallback to reflection during the "is a" tests used by class/annotation scanning by including a small internal index of JDK classes most commonly used. Ideally, this would eliminate the need for any downstream work-around like in [the fix for quarkus 2961](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/commit/cc654c6f0fef16f0f37554ad4d22c7a826ced210#diff-25a0f7545a16a5e105652956c74d3736).
